We believe that the way people interact with their finances will drastically improve in the next few years. We’re dedicated to empowering this transformation by building the tools and experiences that thousands of developers use to create their own products. Plaid powers the tools millions of people rely on to live a healthier financial life. We work with thousands of companies like Venmo, SoFi, several of the Fortune 500, and many of the largest banks to make it easy for people to connect their financial accounts to the apps and services they want to use. Plaid’s network covers 12,000 financial institutions across the US, Canada, UK and Europe. Founded in 2013, the company is headquartered in San Francisco with offices in New York, Seattle, Washington D.C., Raleigh, London, and Amsterdam.
ABOUT THE TEAM
Our Connectivity team owns how Plaid connects to the financial system. We bring banks, credit unions, and other data partners onto the Plaid network and build the integrations every Plaid product runs on. AI is changing how that work gets done. We now build integrations with no human in the loop and are teaching them to fix themselves when they break, which lets us go further: reaching data beyond banks, making the data more complete, and working with partners on letting people and their agents act on their accounts, not just share data.
As a Product Manager for Connectivity Platform, you'll own the platform capabilities that keep Plaid's data supply reliable and efficient, and you'll decide which ones we build as the network evolves. You'll drive the discovery that finds the highest-value work, own the roadmap, and partner closely with engineering to weigh technical trade-offs against business value. You'll work as a true peer to our best engineers and make the hard calls with them. This role is for someone with rare technical depth who likes building things that don't exist yet.
RESPONSIBILITIES
- Drive discovery to identify, validate, and prioritize platform updates or new services, considering against product team roadmaps, reliability challenges, and data quality
- Define and own the overall Connectivity platform roadmap and strategy with the engineering lead, covering our integration automation platform, migration orchestration platform, and data quality initiatives.
- Future: Build shared observability across regions (US, CA, UK/EU)
- Partner closely with engineering to identify and articulate technical trade offs with business value
- Spend deep time with internal teams that depend on the platform to understand their needs and wants, with the ability to distill the information into actionable requests and raise that to the platform team
- Establish and track key metrics
QUALIFICATIONS:
- 5+ years of product management experience
- Proven track record as an internal product manager: You’ve led technical product initiatives where the user base is internal (and oftentimes other engineers or product teams) from discovery, to roadmap/strategy development, through execution and monitoring. You can speak concretely about what made these initiatives succeed or fail (adoption, metrics, iteration).
- Deep technical fluency: You can hold your own with our best engineers on how large systems are designed, evaluating trade-offs, limitations, and business value. You’re intimately familiar with APIs, reading architectures, and developing technical prototypes with the help of AI assistants.
- Leadership, stakeholder influence, and communication :You should be comfortable working cross-functionally (engineering, data, product) and influencing without direct authority. You must be able to explain complex technical ideas to non-technical stakeholders, drive alignment, and make trade-offs crystal clear with concise and simple written and verbal communication.
"NICE TO HAVE" QUALIFICATIONS:
- Experience in fintech
- Generative AI knowledge and experience
- Prior software engineering experience

Our Fraud team's mission is to help companies detect and prevent fraud using financial network data. We believe that transaction patterns, device signals, and behavioral data are an underleveraged tool in fraud prevention.
The Fraud Strategist is responsible for building and maturing our retro-as-a-service and POC program and driving adoption of our fraud products. The role sits between our data team and the customer (i.e., the role will not build the models, but will need to understand the output well enough to clearly and compellingly present the business case and work with technical stakeholders and customers.)
Responsibilities:
- Own the retro and POC process end-to-end and collaborate with customers and internal stakeholders at Plaid
- Partner closely with customers to help them understand the ROI of Protect and make recommendations for implementing our fraud products
- Drive post-retro follow-through to convert retro results into production usage
- Serve as a feedback loop between customers and product to drive our Protect roadmap
Qualifications:
- 5-10 years of experience in a customer-facing analytical role in fintech, financial services, or a related domain (e.g., software/tech)
- Experience working closely with data science teams
- Experience managing consultative customer engagements where you owned the deliverable and the relationship
- Comfort interpreting ML model output (e.g., precision/recall, score distributions) and explaining it to a non-technical audience
- [Nice to have] Background in data science or ML engineering, particularly on a fraud or risk team
- [Nice to have] Experience in fraud, identity, or risk — either from a fraud prevention vendor, a fraud team at a bank or fintech, or consulting on risk engagements

The Analytics Engineering team owns the full-stack analytics foundation for Plaid's GTM, CGX, NEA and Marketing organizations. We build and maintain the core semantic layer data models (dbt on Databricks), activation layer, and BI surfaces that these teams rely on — and we partner with stakeholders to turn those models into decisions, forecasts, analytics and experiments.
As a Senior Analytics Engineer, you’ll also act as an applied data science partner. In addition to core analytics engineering, you’ll work on predictive modeling, experimentation, lifetime value (LTV), and attribution alongside the broader team.
As a Senior Analytics Engineer on the Marketing pod, you will be the technical owner of Plaid's Marketing data stack. You will build the dbt models, predictive frameworks, and self-serve data products that Marketing leadership uses to plan spend, measure performance, and drive growth.
You'll partner directly with PMM, Growth Marketing, and Marketing leadership to deliver core data models, frameworks, and tools — including LTV, lead scoring, and experimentation tooling — with a north star that aims for prescriptive and production-grade analytics. You'll also help build the AI-powered experiences that let Marketing partners self-serve from our metric layer
Responsibilities
- Own the dbt models and data marts that power Marketing analytics, activation, and reporting.
- Build, validate, and productionize predictive models (lead scoring, LTV, channel attribution, propensity) in partnership with Marketing and GTM stakeholders
- Partner with Marketing leadership on measurement frameworks, experiment design, and spend optimization — translating business questions into analytical answers
- Enable self-serve analytics through AI tools and well-documented semantic models
- Collaborate with ML, Data Engineering, and Ops teams to deliver best-in-class data infrastructure to Marketing
Qualifications
- Bachelor's degree in a quantitative field (CS, Statistics, Economics, Engineering, or equivalent experience)
- 5+ years of proven experience in analytics engineering, data science, or a closely adjacent function
- Advanced SQL and production-grade data modeling experience — dbt strongly preferred
- Python proficiency for modeling and analysis work
- Hands-on experience with a modern cloud warehouse (Databricks, Snowflake, BigQuery, or Redshift)
- Demonstrated experience shipping predictive models or applied ML in a business context
- Prior experience in Marketing Analytics, Growth, or GTM analytics at a SaaS or usage-based technology company
- Strong stakeholder communication and the ability to autonomously drive projects end-to-end

GRC Engineering is how we make all of that scale — turning compliance into code, evidence into telemetry, and audits into a continuous, automated capability.
The Role:
- You will own GRC Engineering at Plaid — a foundational, high-ownership role defining an emerging discipline from the ground up. Today most of our compliance work is manual and point-in-time; you will turn it into an engineered system that is continuous, data-driven, and scalable, and set the technical direction for the field.

- Define the discipline and the architecture — how GRC Engineering works at Plaid, not just execute within it.
- Build the foundation the function runs on — a codified source of truth for controls, policies, and evidence, fed by live pipelines and continuous controls monitoring.
- Be the engineering backbone for Security Assurance & Trust Enablement, Third-Party Ecosystem Risk, and Risk Management
- Make risk visible and data-driven — turning control and risk data into real-time signals for the team and leadership.
- Pioneer where compliance is heading — compliance-agents-as-code in the SDLC, AI- and agent-driven workflows, and machine-readable continuous compliance (FedRAMP 20x).
- This role is perfect for you if:
- You think in systems: you'd rather design the thing that eliminates a whole class of manual work than automate one task at a time.
- You love building and shipping internal tools and solutions that people actually use.
- You're relentlessly curious — you poke, you investigate, and you dig into how controls can silently fail, drift, or get bypassed so you can catch it automatically.
- You treat every roadblock as just an obstacle to route around — you don't back down, because there's always a path.
- You like range — juggling several problems across security, risk, compliance, and engineering beats grinding on a single one.
- You're energized by turning compliance from a documentation exercise into demonstrable, continuous, machine-readable evidence.

- Architect GRC's Engineering Foundation: Build the pipelines and codified source of truth the function runs on — controls, policies, and framework mappings captured as structured, version-controlled data and fed by live control and system state — so one control maps evidence across SOC 2, ISO, NIST, and beyond instead of being re-collected for every audit.
- Build Continuous Controls Monitoring: Automate evidence collection, control testing, and monitoring across cloud and internal systems, and write and tune the detection that flags drift and misconfiguration against baseline — so audit readiness is continuous and gaps surface the moment they appear, not at audit time.
- Turn Data into Risk Signal: Build dashboards and SQL-driven reporting that turn raw control and risk data into KPIs, giving the team and leadership real-time visibility into risk posture.
- Drive Data-Informed Risk Assessments: Conduct security and technology risk assessments and recommend mitigations using data — keeping the risk management program running while cutting its manual overhead.
- Automate Operational Toil: Eliminate the recurring manual work the team carries — evidence pulls, access and vendor reviews, questionnaires, risk-register upkeep, status reporting — with durable automation that gives time back across every workstream.

- Experience conducting security or technology risk assessments and translating findings into data-driven mitigation.

Third-party ecosystem risk is a core part of how we keep Plaid safe—we vet the security of both the vendors we rely on and the customers and partners who connect to our platform, so trust runs in both directions.
Role:
- You will run security risk assessments for Plaid’s third parties end-to-end—from intake and questionnaire through risk rating, findings, and tracked exceptions.
- You will assess the security posture of customers and partners onboarding to the platform with the same rigor we apply to vendors.
- You will keep the third-party risk lifecycle moving—risk tiering, reassessment cadence, remediation follow-through, and a clean, current risk register.
- You will help mature the program—questionnaires, tiering criteria, intake, and runbooks—so reviews get faster and more consistent as volume grows, drawing on how you’ve improved third-party risk programs before.
- You will report on ecosystem risk to Security and cross-functional stakeholders, and operate as an AI power user to raise your own throughput.
Responsibilities:
- Run Vendor Security Risk Assessments: Triage inbound vendor requests, run security reviews scaled to risk tier, rate the risk, and document findings and exceptions. Your assessments keep Plaid from inheriting a vendor’s security gaps and give Procurement, Privacy, and Legal a clear risk signal before contracts are signed.
- Vet Customer and Partner Security Posture: Review the security practices of customers and partners onboarding to the platform, applying the same standards you use for vendors. Your reviews make sure who connects to Plaid meets the bar before they touch data—protecting consumers and the ecosystem.
- Keep the Third-Party Risk Lifecycle Current: Maintain risk tiering, drive reassessments on cadence, chase remediation to closure, and keep the risk register accurate. Your follow-through keeps third-party risk a live, trustworthy picture rather than a point-in-time checkbox.
- Mature the Program: Improve questionnaires, tiering criteria, intake, runbooks, and tooling as review volume grows—bringing patterns from third-party risk programs you’ve matured before. Your work moves the function from ad hoc toward fast, consistent, and scalable.
- Report on Ecosystem Risk: Track assessment cycle times, backlog, open exceptions, and reassessment coverage, and report program health to stakeholders. Your reporting gives leadership real visibility into where third-party risk concentrates.
- Scale Through AI and Tooling: Build and scale AI-assisted workflows for assessment review, questionnaire analysis, and reporting—and share what works. Your approach sets how the team uses AI to handle more reviews without adding headcount.
Qualifications:
Must-haves
- 4+ years of experience in vendor risk management
- Third-party and vendor security risk assessment:
- Experience running security risk assessments of third parties—reviewing questionnaires, SOC 2 and ISO reports, and security documentation, and translating them into a defensible risk rating.
- Familiarity with the third-party risk lifecycle: intake, tiering, exceptions and risk acceptance, remediation tracking, and periodic reassessment.
- Security and compliance knowledge:
- Working knowledge of SOC 2, ISO 27001, NIST CSF, and common control domains (access control, encryption, incident response, BC/DR).
- Ability to read a control environment and tell a real gap from an acceptable compensating control.
- Program maturation and operational execution:
- Experience maturing a third-party or vendor risk program—improving how it works (tiering criteria, questionnaires, workflow, automation), not just executing an existing one.
- Track record running assessments at volume without dropping rigor.
- Strong analytical and documentation skills: clear findings, clean tracking, and defensible risk decisions others can follow.
- Communication and cross-functional effectiveness:
- Clear written and verbal communication—able to explain a security risk to Procurement, Legal, or a customer without overstating or hand-waving.
- Comfortable working across Security, Legal, Procurement, and GTM as the third-party risk point of contact.
- AI fluency and tooling:
- Demonstrated ability to apply AI tooling to assessment review, questionnaire analysis, and reporting to materially increase throughput—and to share what works with the team.
Nice-to-have
- A third-party-risk or audit credential (CTPRP, CISA, or CISSP), or hands-on ownership of a TPRM platform (e.g. OneTrust, ProcessUnity, Whistic, SecurityScorecard) beyond using it as an end user.

The Security Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) team is part of Plaid’s security organization, focused on enabling the business by proactively managing information security risks and maintaining effective controls.
Our mission is to reduce the likelihood and impact of security risks while operating a robust assurance program that builds trust with our customers, consumers, and data partners.We partner closely across the company to ensure Plaid’s platform remains secure, resilient, and aligned with industry and regulatory expectations.Security risk management is how Plaid makes informed security trade-offs—we identify and analyze the risks that could materially affect the business, make sure the right owners decide what to do about them, and turn that picture into reporting leadership and the board can act on.
ABOUT THE ROLE:
- You will run security risk assessments end-to-end within Plaid’s security risk management program—intake, scenario-based analysis, treatment decisions, and monitoring across security, infrastructure, and product risk.
- You will work with engineering SMEs and risk owners on risks ranging from over-privileged access and supply-chain gaps to product abuse and AI adoption, giving owners a clear, defensible basis for accepting or mitigating each one.
- You will build quarterly security risk reporting and the security risk content in leadership and board materials.
- You will help integrate security risk into enterprise risk management, so it is tracked and weighed alongside the rest of the business.
- You will help mature the program as its scope grows, and operate as an AI power user who automates the work so it scales.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
- Run Security Risk Assessments: Triage intake, run scenario-based risk analyses with engineering SMEs, score initial and residual risk, and drive risk owners to a documented treatment decision. Your analysis turns vague concerns into decisions leadership can stand behind.
- Build Quarterly Risk Reporting: Gather updates on material risks, prepare the Security Risk Review, and build the security risk content for executive and board decks. Your reporting gives leadership a clear, current view of where security risk sits and what’s being done about it.
- Integrate Security Risk into ERM: Partner with enterprise risk stakeholders to map security risks into the enterprise taxonomy, align rating scales, and keep the registers in sync. Your work puts security risk alongside business risk instead of in a silo.
- Mature the Program: Help evolve the risk framework, register, key risk indicators, and risk-owner self-service as the program’s scope grows. Your work moves the program from tracking risks to measuring and reducing them.
- Support FedRAMP 20x Risk Decisions: Help make sure unmet FedRAMP rules and KSI gaps carry a documented risk explanation and senior-official acceptance in the Security Decision Record, consistent with the risk register. Your work keeps Plaid’s FedRAMP risk posture defensible to agencies and assessors.
- Scale Through AI and Automation: Build AI skills and automations for intake triage, first-draft risk analyses, register hygiene, and report generation—and share them across the team. Your approach lets the program cover more risk without adding headcount.

- Security risk assessment:
- Experience running scenario-based analyses of technical risks (cloud, IAM, software supply chain, application and product) using NIST SP 800-30, FAIR, or a comparable method.
- Technical depth to engage engineers on architecture and controls, and to tell a real exposure from a hypothetical one.
- Risk program maturity and ERM integration:
- Experience building or maturing a security risk program—methodology, register, treatment and exception workflow, and key risk indicators.
- Experience integrating security risk into an enterprise risk management program.
- Risk reporting and executive communication:
- Experience preparing quarterly risk reporting and building security risk content for executive and board decks.
- Ability to turn technical risk into a concise executive narrative without overstating or hand-waving.
- Security and compliance knowledge:

About the Team
The Fraud team is building the largest network of trusted identities in the US. We help customers onboard legitimate users and stop bad actors before they cause downstream harm. Our products span the risk lifecycle: Identity Verification and Monitor for onboarding and compliance, and Protect, our fraud intelligence platform.
We are extending that network to AI agents. Agents are starting to open accounts, link accounts, move money, and transfer between wallets for consumers. The protocols forming around them standardize how an agent identifies itself and what it may do, and leave the question of whether to trust it to the business on the receiving end. Agent Trust, our Know Your Agent (KYA) product, answers it, on top of the identity, consent, and risk infrastructure Plaid already runs.
You will take over Agent Trust: the decision on whether an action an AI agent takes on a financial account can be trusted. You will define how Plaid identifies agents, verifies the people behind them, and evaluates what they are authorized to do, and how that connects to portable identity, reusable KYC, and consumer permissions. You will sell that decision to financial institutions and to Plaid customers, and you will carry Plaid’s requirements into the standards bodies shaping this space, with the fraud engineering and data teams behind you.
Responsibilities:
- Own the vision, strategy, roadmap, and OKRs for Agent Trust. Decide what Plaid offers, to whom, and how it is packaged and priced.
- Define how Plaid identifies agents, verifies the humans behind them, and evaluates what they are allowed to do, for new accounts and existing ones.
- Connect Agent Trust to portable identity, reusable KYC, and consumer permission management, with the product teams that own those surfaces.
- Work directly with financial institutions and Plaid customers as the product expert: discovery, design partnerships, and GTM enablement.
- Represent Plaid’s product requirements in the industry groups and protocol working groups writing the specs for agent identity and authorization, with Partnerships and Legal.
- Partner with data science and engineering on what the product needs: signals, labels, success metrics, and the requirements that tie them together.
Qualifications:
- 4+ years of product management or equivalent product ownership, with meaningful time in fraud, identity, authentication, or payments risk
- Hands-on depth in identity and authorization protocols (OAuth 2.x and OIDC, FIDO and WebAuthn, FDX or Open Banking consent), or in bot, device, and agent detection systems
- Track record of growing a new product line, from early design partners and first customers to repeatable sales
- Experience building with and selling to enterprise customers or financial institutions
- Clear writing, and the ability to translate between protocol engineers, data scientists, GTM, and executives

ABOUT THE ROLE
As the Manager of Machine Learning Engineering on the Credit team, you’ll lead the team responsible for Plaid’s LendScore and Income Insights products. You’ll manage and develop a team of Machine Learning Engineers and Data Scientists, set direction for advancing our insights, and partner with Engineering, Product, and other Data teams to deliver customer and business impact.
In this role, you will:
- Lead, support, and develop a team of Machine Learning Engineers and Data Scientists working across credit insights products.
- Set technical and product direction for evolving LendScore and Income Insights, including the team’s machine learning roadmap.
- Partner with Engineering, Product, and Data teams to prioritize opportunities and deliver reliable, scalable solutions.
- Guide the development of machine learning models across the full lifecycle, from experimentation and offline training to online serving and monitoring.
- Help the team tackle both 0-to-1 opportunities and the scaling and improvement of established products.
- Foster a high-ownership, bottom-up team culture grounded in data-driven decisions and business impact.
WHAT EXCITES YOU
- Leading work that can expand access to financial services for millions of people through well-known and emerging fintech applications.
- Developing products and insights that support the next wave of cash-flow-based underwriting.
- Helping a talented team experiment with modern machine learning techniques and bring them into production.
- Shaping a roadmap that spans new 0-to-1 opportunities and scaling solutions that are already delivering value.
- Working across Data, Engineering, and Product in a high-ownership environment where the team’s work can drive meaningful impact.
WHAT EXCITES US
- 8+ years of experience training and serving AI or machine learning models in production environments.
- Experience leading a team of Data Scientists and Machine Learning Engineers.
- Experience in fintech lending and a strong understanding of how models are built and used in lending.
- Experience building or working with data-intensive backend applications in large, distributed systems.
- Ability to code and iterate independently using data infrastructure tools such as Python, Spark, Jupyter notebooks, and standard machine learning libraries.
- A track record of taking ownership and driving projects to business impact.
- Ability to work effectively with both technical and non-technical teams.
- Master’s degree or equivalent work experience in Computer Science, Mathematics, Engineering, or a closely related field.
- Nice to have: Experience in data analytics or data engineering.
